header.title: Open 2D Studio
header.heroAlt: Open 2D Studio with the floor plan of a fictitious garden office: hatched walls, window and door frames, furniture, dimensions and room names with floor areas
header.label: 2D drafting
header.tagline: From the first line to a print-ready sheet, right in the browser
header.desc: Draw floor plans, details and technical drawings with the tools you know from CAD: layers, snapping, dimensions and hatches. Place your drawing to scale on a sheet with a title block, then print it or save it as PDF or DXF.

meta.description: Free 2D drafting app in the browser: draw floor plans and details with layers, snapping, dimensions and hatches, place them on a sheet with a title block and export to PDF, DXF, SVG or IFC.
meta.title: Open 2D Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

edit.alt: Meeting table with four chairs selected in the floor plan, with grips on each circle and the properties colour, lineweight, line style and radius on the right
edit.title: Draw the way you are used to in CAD
edit.desc: Line, polyline, rectangle, circle, arc, ellipse and spline, with snapping to endpoint, midpoint, centre and intersection. Move, copy, rotate, mirror, trim or fillet, and adjust colour, lineweight and line style in the properties panel.

layers.alt: Layer list opened from the status bar with the layers Walls, Frames, Furniture, Dimensions and Text, each with its own colour and buttons for visibility and locking
layers.title: Layers keep your drawing clear
layers.desc: Put walls, frames, furniture and dimensions each on their own layer with their own colour. Switch a layer off to work without it for a while, or lock it so you don't draw on it by accident.

hatch.alt: Hatch pattern manager with the built-in patterns, with Concrete selected showing a preview and its description
hatch.title: A hatch for every material
hatch.desc: Choose from 47 built-in patterns, from diagonal and cross-hatching to concrete, or make your own pattern. Keep your favourites, and import and export patterns to share them with colleagues.

sheet.alt: A3 sheet with the floor plan at 1:50 in a viewport and a filled-in title block with drawing title, number A-101, project and date
sheet.title: From drawing to sheet with a title block
sheet.desc: Place your drawing to scale on a sheet from A4 to A0, portrait or landscape. Fill in the title block with title, drawing number, project, scale and date, or start from a sheet template.

print.alt: Print dialog with paper size, print range, margins and a preview of the floor plan, with the buttons Export PDF and Print
print.title: Print or save as PDF
print.desc: Choose the paper size, portrait or landscape, the margins and what to print: the current view or a selection of sheets. You see a preview straight away, and save your settings as a preset for next time.

ifc.alt: IFC Model panel below the floor plan with the IFC4 text that is built live from the drawing, with the buttons Copy and Export .ifc
ifc.title: Works with other CAD and BIM software
ifc.desc: Read and write DXF for AutoCAD, BricsCAD and other CAD programs, and export to SVG, JSON and IFC4. The IFC panel shows live how your drawing is written out as IFC.

notice.text: The browser version works straight away. The desktop and Android apps are not yet available for public download, and the latest version (v0.35) dates from March 2026.

lines.desc: Straight or smooth, open or closed.

shapes.title: Rectangle, circle, arc and ellipse

layers.title: Layers
layers.desc: With colour, visibility and locking per layer.

find.title: Find and replace

dims.title: Dimensions
dims.desc: Aligned, linear, angular, radius and diameter.

sheets.title: Several drawings and sheets
sheets.desc: Keep plan, section and details together in one file.

title.title: Title block

print.title: Printing and PDF
print.desc: With preview, margins and saved presets.

units.title: Units and scale

dxf.title: Open and save DXF
dxf.desc: Exchange drawings with AutoCAD, BricsCAD and other CAD programs.

underlay.title: Underlay

image.title: Images

export.title: SVG, JSON and IFC4
export.desc: For the web, your own scripts or a BIM model.

project.title: Own project file
project.desc: All drawings, sheets and layers together in one .o2d file.

ext.desc: Browse, install and update extensions from the menu.

themes.title: Seven colour themes

features.label: Features

themes.title: Colour themes

settings.title: Settings are kept

whatsnew.label: New in v0.35
whatsnew.title: Your own colours and extensions
whatsnew.desc: The latest releases, from v0.30 to v0.35 in March 2026, brought colour themes, a cleaner interface, extensions and feedback from within the app.

files.a: Your own project files (.o2d) and DXF files from AutoCAD, BricsCAD or another CAD program. You can use a PDF or a large DXF file as an underlay, and insert images. Open 2D Studio does not open DWG files yet; save them as DXF in your CAD program first.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The browser version works straight away, without an account. There are also versions for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android tablets, but they are not yet available for public download.

price.a: Nothing. You pay no licence fee and need no account or subscription.

save.q: In what format is my work saved?
save.a: As an .o2d project file, with all your drawings, sheets and layers. In the browser you download that file. You can also export to DXF, SVG, JSON and IFC4, and to PDF via the print dialog.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: In any modern browser on Windows, macOS and Linux. Desktop versions for Windows, macOS and Linux and an Android app for tablets exist, but are not public yet.

practice.a: You work in millimetres at a scale such as 1:50 or 1:100, with paper sizes from A4 to A0, a title block, and text and dimensions in an ISO typeface. The interface is in English for now.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: Every draw, modify and layer command is described as a tool for AI assistants. In the desktop version you type a request in plain language in the terminal, such as "draw a circle", and Claude Code on your own computer carries it out. This does not work in the browser yet, and there is no MCP server to connect to yourself yet.

cad.q: How is it different from Open CAD Studio?
cad.a: They are two separate programs by different makers. Open CAD Studio is built to open and update DWG and DXF files from others, in 2D and 3D. Open 2D Studio focuses on drawing in 2D yourself: layers, dimensions, hatches and sheets with a title block. If you mostly work with DWG files from others, take a look at Open CAD Studio.

source.a: Not yet. Open 2D Studio carries the LGPL-3.0 licence, but its GitHub repository is not public yet. That is why this page has no downloads yet.

status.q: Is it still being worked on?
status.a: The latest version, v0.35, dates from March 2026. The browser version went online in April; since then there have only been small maintenance changes. If you miss something, report it with F1 in the app.

tauri.desc: A thin native shell in Rust for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, with an installer of a few megabytes.

react.desc: The interface in separate components with type checking; Zustand keeps track of the drawing state.

canvas.desc: Own drawing engine on the HTML canvas, with snapping, grips and selection.

dxf.desc: Own DXF reader and writer in TypeScript, so exchange works in the browser too.

pdf.desc: Vector PDF for printing, and reading PDF files as an underlay.

osifont.desc: Open typeface to ISO 3098 for text and dimensions.
